out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Test Kit/Device Used to Check Sanitizer Conc
violations.observation: The operator is not testing the chemical sanitizing solution to ensure proper concentration of the solution.
violations.corrective_action: The operator shall be monitoring the concentration of the sanitizing solution using a test kit or other device. EHS educated on proper test kit use. Must dip for 10 seconds only

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: lettuce and cabbage 45- 49f in standing refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC ensured vegetables were stored in the fridge the entire day after the arrived at 10am. Check delivery temperatures to ensure food arrives 41f. CDI Food will be returned for refund.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: cooling canned beans on salad bar in plastic containers. Then cooling after lunch service in refrigerator with lid on.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI cool food in refrigerator before service, cool items without lid on, pre cool can in refrigerator overnight recommended.

out_items.name: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding

violations.title: Reheating for Hot Holding, Temp Reached within 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following food item(s) was not reheated for hot holding within a sufficient time of 2 hours or less: leftover burgers are placed from the refrigerator straight into the warming hot cabinet to reheat.
violations.corrective_action: Reheating food for hot holding shall be done rapidly, within 2 hours to prevent growth of pathogens. Leftover foods must be reheated in oven or steamer to 165f and 135f for commercially packaged foods reheated the first time. CDI discarded

violations.title: Reheating for Hot Holding, Proper Temp
violations.observation: The following food item(s) was not reheated for hot holding to a sufficient temperature and/or time: leftover burgers reheating in the oven to 135f
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated to a minimum temperature of 165F for 15 seconds. CDI discarded.

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked properly: cooked potato wedges date marked for 10/16/25-10/31/25
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. CDI item date marked to 10/22/25 SILVERBROOK ELEMENTARY SCHOOL (Inspection Date: 10/17/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: cooling room temperature lettuce in tightly packed plastic container with the lid on.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI lid removed to allow cold airflow/cooling.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: observed frozen pizzas on rack at 63f thawing outside of refrigeration.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. CDI placed in refrigerator.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: yogurt containers used to store onions, and other food items.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. CDI labeled.
